gloss: to drink up; to drain; to finish a drink

definitions.gloss: to drink up; to drain; to finish a drink
definitions.explanation: To drink a beverage completely, emptying the container without leaving any liquid behind.

examples.japanese: ⟦ビール→ビール：01015_biiru⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{一気|いっき}→一気：08891_ikki⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{飲|の}み{干|ほ}した。
examples.english: I drained the beer in one gulp.

examples.japanese: ⟦{冷|つめ}たい→冷たい：00681_tsumetai⟧⟦{水|みず}→水：02258_mizu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦コップ→コップ：00862_koppu⟧⟦{一杯|いっぱい}→一杯：01793_ippai⟧{飲|の}み{干|ほ}した。
examples.english: I drank up a whole glass of cold water.

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{残|のこ}っていた→残る：01187_nokoru⟧⟦ワイン→ワイン：01067_wain⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{最後|さいご}→最後：01413_saigo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{一滴|いってき}→一滴：08893_itteki⟧⟦まで→まで：00490_made⟧{飲|の}み{干|ほ}して⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦グラス→グラス：00076_gurasu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{置|お}いた→置く：01092_oku⟧。
examples.english: He drained the remaining wine to the last drop before setting down his glass.

notes:
A compound verb formed from ⟦{飲|の}む→飲む：00322_nomu⟧ (to drink) + ⟦{干|ほ}す→干す：00115_hosu⟧ (to dry out). The ⟦{干|ほ}す→干す：00115_hosu⟧ component adds the meaning of completely finishing or emptying a container of liquid.

USAGE:
- Emphasizes drinking everything without leaving any behind
- Often used with ⟦{一気|いっき}→一気：08891_ikki⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧ (in one go) for dramatic effect
- Can imply a bold or determined manner of drinking

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦ビール→ビール：01015_biiru⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{飲|の}み{干|ほ}す: to drain a beer
- ⟦{一気|いっき}→一気：08891_ikki⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{飲|の}み{干|ほ}す: to chug; to drain in one gulp
- ⟦{最後|さいご}→最後：01413_saigo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{一滴|いってき}→一滴：08893_itteki⟧⟦まで→まで：00490_made⟧{飲|の}み{干|ほ}す: to drink to the last drop
- ⟦グラス→グラス：00076_gurasu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{飲|の}み{干|ほ}す: to empty a glass

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{飲|の}む→飲む：00322_nomu⟧: the basic verb for drinking; does not imply finishing
- ⟦{飲|の}み{切|き}る→飲み切る：26965_nomikiru⟧: to drink completely; similar meaning but less vivid
- がぶ{飲|の}み⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to gulp down; emphasizes the rough manner of drinking rather than completeness
